exclusions.query: Apply the nonzero determinant count directly to collinear triples.

outputs.exact_statement:
There are absolute constants $\eta,c_1>0$ and an integer $n_0\ge3$ such that $$\Delta(n)\ge c_1n^{-2+\eta}
 \qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge n_0.$$

For a lattice $L$ of positive rank $s$ and the lengths just defined, $$\det L\le\prod_{i=1}^s\lambda_i\le s^{s/2}\det L.$$ Consequently, the lattice generated by $v_1,\ldots,v_s$ has index at most $s^{s/2}$ in $L$.

Let $L$ be a rank-two Euclidean lattice with successive lengths $\lambda_1\le\lambda_2$. If $R\ge\lambda_2$, any translate of $L$ has at most $C R^2/\det L$ points in any ball of radius $R$. If $R<\lambda_2$, the points of $L$ in the ball of radius $R$ centered at zero lie in a line and number at most $1+2R/\lambda_1$.

Let $y\in\mathbb Z^3$ be primitive, meaning that its coordinates have greatest common divisor one. Then $L_y=\mathbb Z^3\cap y^\perp$ has determinant $|y|$. More generally, if $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^3$ is a full-rank lattice of index $I$ and $y\cdot\Lambda=g\mathbb Z$ with $g>0$, then $$\det(\Lambda\cap y^\perp)=\frac{I|y|}{g}.$$

Let $R_1\ge R_2\ge R_3\ge1$ and let $t\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$. The number of triples $u_1,u_2,u_3\in\mathbb Z^3$ satisfying $|u_j|\le R_j$ and $\det(u_1,u_2,u_3)=t$ is at most $$C(R_1R_2R_3)^2\bigl(\log(2R_1)\bigr)^2.$$ The constant is independent of $t$ and of the three radii.

Let $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^3$ have index $I$, let $X\ge2$, and suppose its third successive length satisfies $\lambda_3\le X$. For every $t\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, the number of $3$ by $3$ matrices with rows in $\Lambda$, row lengths at most $X$, and determinant $t$ is at most $$C\bigl(\log(2X)\bigr)^2\frac{X^6}{I^2}.$$ The constant is absolute.
For every sufficiently large integer $n$, there is a prime $p$ with $n<p\le2n$.

Let $C$ be a matrix of three columns constructed by [norm:column], with labels $\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3$. If these labels are distinct, then the residue $\det C\in R_h$ has no integer representative in $[-\tau,\tau]$.

Let $C\in M_3(R_h)$ have at least one unit entry. There are invertible matrices $P,Q\in\operatorname{GL}_3(R_h)$ and integers $0\leq b\leq e\leq k$ such that $$C=P\,\operatorname{diag}(1,B^b,B^e)\,Q.$$ Set $D=B^b$, $E=B^e$, and $I=DE$, all as positive integers. The subgroup $$\Lambda_C=\{v\in\mathbb Z^3:
       v\bmod h\text{ belongs to the row span of }C\}$$ is a full lattice satisfying $$=I,
 \qquad E\mathbb Z^3\subseteq\Lambda_C.
 \label{orb:lattice}$$ Moreover, $b\geq j$, for $1\leq j\leq k$, if and only if every $2\times2$ minor of $C$ vanishes modulo $B^j$.

Under the hypotheses and notation of Lemma 10, define $$\mathcal O_C=\{GC:G\in\operatorname{SL}_3(R_h)\}.$$ There is an absolute constant $c_0>0$ such that $$|\mathcal O_C|\geq c_0\frac{h^8}{D^3E^2}. \label{orb:orbit-bound}$$ For a uniformly chosen $G\in\operatorname{SL}_3(R_h)$, the matrix $GC$ is uniform on $\mathcal O_C$. Every matrix in this orbit has the same row span and determinant as $C$.

Let $r,L$ be positive integers with $r\geq2$, $r\mid L$, and $L10, and put $\theta=B(r/L)^4$. Then, for every $1\leq j\leq k$, $$\Pr(b\geq j\mid\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3) \leq(r/L)^{4j}. \label{orb:tail}$$ If $\theta<1$, then $$\mathbb E[D\mid\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3] \leq1+\sum_{j=1}^k\theta^j \leq\frac1{1-\theta}. \label{orb:moment}$$

Let $q$ be an odd prime and $1\le w\le q$ an integer. There is a set $S\subset\{0,\ldots,w-1\}^3\subset\mathbb F_q^3$ with $|S|\ge w^3/q$ such that no affine line contains three distinct points of $S$.

Let $H\ge1$ be an integer, let $q\ge2000H^2$ be prime, and put $w=\lfloor q/(1000H^2)\rfloor$. Suppose $S\subset\{0,\ldots,w-1\}^3$ contains no three distinct collinear points. The set $\mathcal A$ in [aux:allowed-shifts] has at least $q^3/2$ elements. For every $a\in\mathcal A$ and every invertible $G_q$, the set $V$ in [aux:set-definition] has $|S|$ elements, does not contain zero, and contains no three distinct collinear points.* *Moreover, let $x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ satisfy $|x|\le H$, where $|x|$ is the Euclidean norm. For any $u^{(1)},u^{(2)},u^{(3)}\in V$, the relation $$\label{aux:short-relation} x_1u^{(1)}+x_2u^{(2)}+x_3u^{(3)}=0 \quad\text{in }\mathbb F_q^3$$ is impossible if $x_1+x_2+x_3\ne0$. If $x_1+x_2+x_3=0$, it is impossible whenever the three columns are affinely independent. Consequently, [aux:short-relation] is impossible for three distinct elements of $V$.

For the distribution in [aux:set-definition], with $s=|S|\ge1$, the following bounds hold with absolute constants: $$\label{aux:weight-bounds} \begin{aligned} W(A)&\ll1 &&\text{if the columns of }A\bmod q\text{ are affinely independent},\\ W(A)&\ll q^3/s &&\text{if }\operatorname{rank}(A\bmod q)\ge2,\\ W(A)&\ll(q^3/s)^2 &&\text{for every }A. \end{aligned}$$ If $W(A)>0$, no column of $A\bmod q$ is zero, and its columns are either affinely independent or include two equal columns. For an affinely independent triple with $W(A)>0$, there is no nonzero $x\in\mathbb Z^3$ with $|x|\le H$ and $Ax=0\bmod q$.

For two sampled columns $u,v$, one has $$\label{sam:pair-bound}
 \Pr\bigl(\pi(u)=\pi(v)\bigr)\ll (hq)^6N^{-3}.$$

Three sampled columns satisfy $$\label{sam:triple-bound}
 \Pr\bigl(\pi(u^{(1)}),\pi(u^{(2)}),\pi(u^{(3)})
       \text{ are pairwise distinct},\ |\det A|\le\tau\bigr)
 \ll (\log(2N))^2\frac{h}{N^3r^d}.$$

For a primitive vector $x\in\mathbb Z^3$, put $$\Lambda_x=\Lambda\cap x^\perp,\qquad
 x\cdot\Lambda=g(x)\mathbb Z,\qquad
 J_x=\det(\Lambda_x),$$ where $g(x)>0$. Then $$\label{zero:plane-data}
 g(x)\mid E,\qquad J_x=\frac{I|x|}{g(x)},\qquad
 \frac{g(x)^3}{I}\le h^2.$$ The reduction of $\Lambda_x$ modulo $q$ is the entire plane $$\Pi_x=\{v\in\mathbb F_q^3:v\cdot\bar x=0\},
 \qquad \bar x=x\bmod q\ne0.$$ If $\Gamma\subseteq\Lambda_x$ is a sublattice of index $m$, the number of ordered triples of vectors in $\Gamma$, all of length at most $4N$ and spanning a plane over $\mathbb Q$, is at most $$\label{zero:row-count}
 \ll \frac{N^6}{(mJ_x)^3}.$$

For $R\ge h$, $$\label{zero:moment-bound}
 \sum_{\substack{x\in\mathbb Z^3\ \mathrm{primitive}\\
                  R\le |x|<2R}}g(x)^3
 \ll R^3 I.$$ In particular, this estimate holds when $R>H/2$.
